maxGraceDays.text: Days a non-compliant device keeps access before action is taken

report.title: {Items.Count} compliance {Plural(Items.Count, 'policy allows', 'policies allow')} more than {params.maxGraceDays} days before acting

messages.businessImpact: A device found unencrypted or unpatched keeps its access for weeks, which is long enough for the exposure the check was meant to close.
remediation: Reduce the grace period to a small number of days.
Add an earlier action that emails the user, so being marked non-compliant is never the first they hear of it.
messages.cannotSee: The grace period is taken as the longest of the policy's scheduled actions, so a policy that marks a device non-compliant late but warns early is judged on the later one. What happens to a non-compliant device is a Conditional Access question rather than a compliance one, and a tenant whose policies grant access to non-compliant devices anyway is not judged here. Compliance authored in the Settings Catalog is not read at all.
